[word/document.xml] The nominal 4 ft x 8 ft sideline screen provides the color guard with a concealed area for storing equipment and making costume or equipment changes. The frame is constructed from 3/4-in. EMT conduit, off-the-shelf brackets, and 3D-printed parts. Decorative vinyl covers the finished face. The completed screen folds flat for transport and storage and unfolds for field deployment.

[word/document.xml] Field Operations

-[word/document.xml] Appendix A is the field-facing portion of the manual. It is designed to be printed and carried independently by operators responsible for transport, deployment, inspection, ballasting, and storage.

-[word/document.xml] Section status: The procedures below are development notes, not a complete field-use procedure. Deployment sequence, approved ballast quantity, and operating limits still require validation.
-[word/document.xml] Folding and transport

-[word/document.xml] To prepare sideline screens for transport, handlers release the hinged arm clips, fold the bottom support arms (E) upward against the rear frame, and collapse the entire rear support frame flat against the main frame. Multiple folded screens are loaded vertically onto a dedicated rolling transport cart between side guide rails. Front and rear retaining gates are closed and latched (Cart Gate Latch) to lock screens in place during transit from the equipment trailer to the stadium entrance.
-[word/document.xml] Deployment and Sideline Cart Stowage

-[word/document.xml] At the performance field gate, the transport cart is rolled to the sideline staging position. Handlers unlatch and open the front and back cart gates, lift individual folded screens from the cart bed, and carry them to their designated sideline coordinates. Once on coordinate, operators swing the rear support frame open and snap the hinged arm clips securely over the bottom support arms (E). During the performance, the empty transport cart remains parked and braked along the sideline outside the performance boundary. Immediately upon the final performance cue, screens are collapsed flat, rapidly reloaded into the transport cart, gates latched, and the cart rolled off the field in continuous movement per Rule 8.05.
-[word/document.xml] Ballasting

-[word/document.xml] The current design allows ballast to be suspended from upper weight clips. Placing weights over the bottom support components may fatigue or break the 3D-printed hinged arm clips and is not an approved method until load testing is complete.

-[word/document.xml] Do not issue for field use: Before this subsection is released, specify the approved weight clips, ballast quantity, attachment locations, wind limits, inspection criteria, and response to changing weather.
-[word/document.xml] Applicable 2026 Marching Band Competition & Prop Rules

-[word/document.xml] The following governing rules are extracted directly from the official 2026 Colorado Bandmasters Association (CBA) Marching Band Rulebook (Appendix B Index [11]). All prop builders, parent crew, and student field operators must adhere to these standards:

-[word/document.xml] ANNUAL RULEBOOK NOTICE: This section reflects the governing rules for the 2026 competitive season. Logistics staff and build leads must review this section annually against updated CBA and Bands of America (BOA) rulebooks to verify continuing compliance.
-[word/document.xml] Rule 8.05: Props, Equipment, Surface Protection, and Double-Bagging
-[word/document.xml] • Gate Ingress: All props and equipment must be designed and of a quantity such that they can be brought onto the Performance Field from the band entrance gate.
-[word/document.xml] • Continuous Movement: Following the end of the band's Performance, all props and equipment must be in continuous movement until entirely removed from the stadium.

-[word/document.xml] • Turf Contact Protection: All wooden props must be protected with a heavy-duty sustainable plastic product (PVC, Melamine, etc.) where said prop comes in contact with the field surface. Steel props with smooth edges are acceptable without the need for additional protection.

-[word/document.xml] • Secondary Containment for Sandbags: Props must not leave holes in the Performance Field surface. Sand bags must be in a secondary container (bucket, double bagged, etc.) that will prevent sand from leaking.
-[word/document.xml] Rule 8.07: Equipment Wheel and Turf Protection Standards

-[word/document.xml] • Pneumatic-Like Tires: All instruments and equipment wheeled into the stadium from the entrance gate forward must have pneumatic-like tires. Wheels must be able to support the weight of the instrument/prop without creating damage to the field surface.
-[word/document.xml] Rule 8.08: Prop Staging Height Restrictions

-[word/document.xml] • 12-Foot Rigid Height Limit: Staging (props, backdrops, screens, or similar objects) built and/or used by bands at CBA sanctioned events shall be limited to a maximum total height of twelve (12) feet, including wheels, platforms, and safety railings. Materials such as wood, metal, plastic, or aluminum are not permitted above the twelve-foot limit. (Note: The Sideline Screen is a nominal 4 ft height when deployed, safely conforming to this rule).
-[word/document.xml] Rule 8.09: Prop Assembly, Timing, and USAFA Falcon Stadium Clearance

-[word/document.xml] • Staging Ingress: A band may bring props into the stadium after the previous band has entered the field. Props must fit in the end zone curve without blocking entrance/exit gates.

-[word/document.xml] • Falcon Stadium 9'6" Tunnel Rule: Any prop being used at Falcon Stadium (United States Air Force Academy) must not exceed 9 ft 6 in. to clear the tunnel entrance. Props up to the 12-ft limit may be erected in the tunnel after clearing the initial entrance.

-[word/document.xml] • Falcon Stadium Venue Update (2025/2026): While the 9'6" tunnel restriction remains in the printed CBA rulebook, it has been rendered obsolete by stadium renovations completed prior to the 2025 season. The lower overhead crossbeam at the bottom of the Falcon Stadium tunnel was permanently removed, allowing props to clear without restriction.
-[word/document.xml] Rule 9.07: Parent Field Access & Wristband Limits

-[word/document.xml] • 25 Field Pass Wristbands: Access to the field is restricted to Directors/Staff with CBA passes and parents assisting with props/front ensemble with designated Field Pass wristbands. Each band receives exactly 25 Field Pass wristbands upon check-in. Additional wristbands are not available.
-[word/document.xml] Post-use inspection and storage

-[word/document.xml] This subsection will cover ballast removal, damage checks, drying and cleaning, folding, transport, storage position, and reporting damaged brackets, conduit, vinyl, or printed parts.

+[word/document.xml] Appendix A is the field-facing portion of the manual. It is designed to be printed and carried independently by student field operators, parent pit crew, and logistics handlers responsible for transport, field staging, deployment, ballasting, and safety abort protocols.
+[word/document.xml] 1.1 Folding, Transport, and Rolling Cart Loading

+[word/document.xml] • Fully Assembled Transport: Unlike rolling backdrops, Sideline Screens (Duck Blinds) are transported FULLY ASSEMBLED. They require zero mechanical assembly, bolt fastening, or pin insertion at the competition venue. All frame hinges and clips remain permanently connected.

+[word/document.xml] • Rapid Folding Sequence: To fold a deployed screen flat for transport, handlers disengage the two 3D-printed hinged arm clips (I) from the lower inner cross rail (Rail 3), swing the bottom support arms (E) upward against the rear frame, and collapse the entire rear support frame (D/C) flat against the main frame. The vinyl banner remains taut and undisturbed.

+[word/document.xml] • Dedicated Rolling Cart Loading: Folded screens are loaded vertically onto the dedicated rolling transport cart between side guide rails. Front and rear retaining gates are closed and latched (using the 3D-printed Cart Gate Latches) to lock the stack securely in place for smooth rolling between the equipment trailer and stadium staging areas.
+[word/document.xml] 1.2 Field Routing, Staging, and Rapid 15-Second Deployment

+[word/document.xml] • CBA Rule 5.02 Mandatory Rear Entrance Rule: CRITICAL RULES COMPLIANCE — Even though Sideline Screens are placed along the front sideline flanking the front ensemble, CBA Rule 5.02 strictly mandates that ALL PROPS MUST ENTER THE PERFORMANCE FIELD FROM THE BACK SIDELINE OR REAR END ZONE GATES (above the goal posts). Entering directly across the front boundary is strictly reserved for front ensemble equipment personnel and soloists. Handlers must roll the transport cart through the rear entrance gate and transit along the field perimeter around to their front sideline coordinates. Crossing directly onto the field from the front is a direct boundary violation.

+[word/document.xml] • Front Sideline Placement Coordinates: Screens are positioned along the front sideline to either side of the front ensemble (pit): Side 1 (Left) between the 25 and 42-yard lines, and Side 2 (Right) between the 58 and 75-yard lines. Screens conceal auxiliary color guard equipment, prop flags, quick-change items, and auxiliary instruments.

+[word/document.xml] • 15-Second Field Deployment Sequence: 1) Unlatch cart gates; 2) Handlers remove folded screens from cart; 3) Carry to marked yard line coordinates; 4) Swing rear support frame open; 5) Snap the two hinged arm clips (I) firmly onto the lower inner cross rail (Rail 3); 6) Deploy required sandbag ballast over rear ground rail C. Total setup time is under 15 seconds per screen.
+[word/document.xml] 1.3 Handler Training & High-Wind Emergency Abort Protocol

+[word/document.xml] • Crew Sizing: Each sideline screen is handled by no fewer than two student operators during field transit and placement. On steep inclines (Falcon Stadium concrete tunnel ramp) or breezy days, assign 3 to 4 handlers to the transport cart.

+[word/document.xml] • High-Wind Field Abort (Tier 4 Thresholds): If sustained winds exceed 20 mph or peak gusts exceed 25 mph, field operations are STRICT NO-GO. If sudden severe gusts strike while on the field, handlers immediately disengage the two hinged arm clips (I), fold the rear support frame flat against the main frame, and lay the entire screen flat on the turf. Per CBA Rule 4.02(a), authorized adult volunteers with Rule 9.07 Field Pass wristbands may enter the field solely to hold or secure props in dangerous winds.
+[word/document.xml] 1.4 Ballasting System, Tiered Wind Schedule, and Double-Bagging Protocol

+[word/document.xml] The Sideline Screen presents a 4 ft nominal height by 8 ft width (30.5 sq ft actual area; 3.875 ft H x 7.875 ft W). Its center of pressure sits 1.94 ft above the turf. At high altitude (Colorado Springs 6,500 ft ASL), air density is 0.0595 lb/cu ft (~23% less dense than sea level at 0.0765 lb/cu ft).

+[word/document.xml] • Critical Forward-Tipping Asymmetry: The dry frame weighs 26 lbs. For wind from the front (backward tipping about rear ground rail C), the heavy front frame provides 50.4 ft-lb of natural restoring moment, resisting winds up to 18.9 mph without any ballast. However, for wind from the rear (forward tipping about the front bottom rail), the front frame sits directly on the pivot with zero restoring leverage, leaving only 9.2 ft-lb of restoring moment (tipping at just 8.1 mph). Forward tipping is the critical failure mode!

+[word/document.xml] • Engineering Ballast Analysis — Rear Rail C vs. Rail 2 Suspension: 1) Placed over Rear Ground Rail C (Primary Ballast): Placing 15-lb sandbags over rear ground rail C acts at the maximum possible lever arm (the full 2.29 ft base depth). Two 15-lb bags (30 lbs) provide 68.7 ft-lb of restoring moment, boosting forward tipping resistance to 23.5 mph (an 8.5x increase). Crucially, weight placed on rail C bears directly on the turf and imposes ZERO mechanical stress on the 3D-printed clips (I). 2) Suspended from Upper Inner Rail 2: Hanging sandbags from Rail 2 (using 3D-printed Weight Clips) has a near-zero lever arm to the front rail, providing zero resistance against forward tipping. However, it provides a full 2.29 ft lever arm against backward tipping (34.4 ft-lb per bag). Therefore, rear ground rail C is the mandatory primary location; Rail 2 hanging is strictly a high-wind supplemental ballast location for bidirectional balance.

+[word/document.xml] • Mandatory Double-Bagging (CBA Rule 8.05): All sandbags brought onto athletic turf must be double-bagged with intact heavy-duty plastic inner liners. Single-layer sandbags are strictly prohibited to prevent sand leakage onto stadium turf infill.
+[word/document.xml] 1.5 Applicable 2026 Marching Band Competition & Prop Rules

+[word/document.xml] The following governing rules are extracted directly from the official 2026 Colorado Bandmasters Association (CBA) Marching Band Rulebook (archived at PCHSMB/rules/CBA_Marching_Band_Rules.pdf). All field handlers and parent crew must strictly observe these regulations:

+[word/document.xml] • Rule 5.02 (Mandatory Rear Field Entrance for Props): Props must enter the Performance Field from the back of the field or the back half of the end zone. Only front ensemble equipment and soloists are permitted to enter across the front boundary. Sideline screens must enter through rear gates and transit around to front sideline positions.

+[word/document.xml] • Rule 5.03 & 5.06 (Field Entry Permission & Timing): Props and handlers may pre-stage in the rear half of the end zone (from middle of goal post to far sideline) up to the goal line prior to permission. NEVER enter the field until the Timing & Penalties judge gives official permission. Total field time starts upon entry permission.

+[word/document.xml] • Rule 4.03 & 5.06 (Clear Field Before Performance): All adult volunteers assisting with props must be COMPLETELY CLEAR of the performance field before the introductory announcement ends (3:15 after entry permission). Any adult still in the performance area at announcement end incurs an immediate 0.2 point score penalty.

+[word/document.xml] • Rule 4.03 (Re-Entry Prohibition During Performance): Adults are strictly prohibited from entering or re-entering the performance field during the performance (0.2 penalty per occurrence). Adults must remain in designated exterior perimeter staging areas.

+[word/document.xml] • Rule 4.02(c) (Medical Emergency Assistance Exception): NO PENALTY. Any band member becoming ill or injured during a performance may be assisted from the field by an adult volunteer, parent, staff member, emergency medical technician, or CBA official without any score penalty whatsoever.

+[word/document.xml] • Rule 4.02(a) (High-Wind Prop Safety Restraint Exception): In high winds when props are in danger of falling over, adults may be in the performance field solely to secure props (may never move props as part of the visual choreography).

+[word/document.xml] • Rule 8.05 (Continuous Egress & Double-Bagging): Following the performance, all props and equipment must remain in continuous movement until entirely removed from the stadium. NEVER de-ballast or stop carts at the stadium exit chute. Sandbags must be double-bagged.
+[word/document.xml] • Rule 8.07 & 8.08 (Wheels & 12-Foot Height Limit): Pneumatic-like tires required on carts; 12-foot rigid height limit strictly observed (screen is 4 ft height when deployed).
+[word/document.xml] • Rule 9.07 (25 Field Pass Wristbands): Access restricted to designated wristbands (max 25 per band upon check-in; field-only access). Separate colors for Prelims vs Finals.
+[word/document.xml] 1.6 Post-Use Egress, Inspection & Storage

+[word/document.xml] • Continuous Uphill Egress: Upon show conclusion, handlers immediately disengage hinged arm clips (I), collapse screens flat, load onto transport cart, latch retaining gates, and roll the cart off the field in continuous movement up to the trailer staging lot per Rule 8.05. Do not de-ballast or park carts in stadium exit chutes.

+[word/document.xml] • Two-Shot Competition Protocol: Between Prelims and Finals, screens remain stacked on the transport cart in the trailer lot. If afternoon gusts increase, keep screens folded flat on the cart bed to eliminate sail area while maintaining readiness for Finals.

+[word/document.xml] Step 3.1: Cutting Engineered Wind Relief Slits (Optional / High-Wind Venues)

+[word/document.xml] For venues with frequent high-wind conditions (such as Colorado Springs), cutting engineered inverted-U wind relief slits into the upper zone of the vinyl banner significantly enhances aerodynamic stability by bleeding peak gust dynamic pressure and reducing the net drag coefficient from Cd = 1.20 to Cd = 1.02.

+[word/document.xml] • Mandatory Tear-Arrest Relief Holes: NEVER cut a sharp razor corner into scrim vinyl without first punching circular relief holes. Sharp internal corners act as severe stress risers (Kt >= 3.0), leading to banner tearing under wind flutter. Use a sharp 3/8-in. (10 mm) rotary leather punch or gasket punch to create clean circular holes at both upper hinge corners before cutting.

+[word/document.xml] • Crescent Flap Geometry: Cut 4 to 6 inverted-U crescent flaps (6.0 in. to 8.0 in. wide with a 4.0 in. to 5.0 in. downward curved drop) across the upper zone of the banner (between Rail 1 and Rail 2). Gravity keeps the flaps flush and invisible from the audience in calm air, while wind pressure pushes flaps open to vent gusts.
[word/document.xml] Step 4: Long-Side Tensioning and Initial Wrap

[word/document.xml] Start along one designated long side (typically the top A rail). Beginning at the center tape strip and progressing outward toward both corners, fold the vinyl bleed margin tightly around the conduit and press it firmly into the 5 double-sided tape strips on the rear of the tube. Check that the graphic remains aligned with the outer tubing edge.

[word/document.xml] Move to the opposing long side (bottom A rail). Starting at the center and working outward, pull the vinyl firmly across the frame face to eliminate all slack and wrinkles. Fold the vinyl edge tightly around the bottom conduit and press it securely into the 5 opposing tape strips.

+[word/document.xml] 2. Critical On-Field Safety & CBA Routing Rules

+[word/document.xml] • CBA Rule 5.02 Mandatory Rear Entrance: Props must enter strictly from the back sideline or rear end zone gates (above goal posts). +[word/document.xml] • Ballasting Leverage (Rear Rail C): Always deploy primary sandbags over rear ground rail C first for maximum lever arm against rear wind. For Tier 2/3, hang supplemental bags from Rail 2 using 3D-printed Weight Clips.
+[word/document.xml] • Mandatory Double-Bagging (Rule 8.05): All sandbags must have intact heavy-duty plastic inner liners. Never bring single-layer bags onto athletic turf.

+[word/document.xml] • High-Wind Emergency Lay-Flat: If severe gusts strike (>25 mph), handlers disengage hinged arm clips (I), fold rear support frame flat, and lay screens flat on turf. Adult volunteers with Rule 9.07 wristbands may assist per Rule 4.02(a).
+[word/document.xml] 3. Rapid Field Deployment & Teardown Checklist

+[word/document.xml] • Venue Staging & Ingress: Screens are transported fully assembled on cart. Roll cart to rear gate. When T&P judge signals entry permission, roll cart along perimeter to front sideline placement zone.

+[word/document.xml] • 15-Second Deployment & Egress: 1) Unlatch cart gates; 2) Lift screen onto coordinate; 3) Swing rear triangle open; 4) Snap bottom support arms (E) into clips (I) on Rail 3; 5) Place double-bagged sandbags over rear rail C; 6) Clear field before announcement ends. At show conclusion, unclip E arms, fold flat into cart, latch gates, and maintain continuous egress off field up hill to trailer lot per Rule 8.05.
